question: What's Delta's policy on oversold flights?
answer:
Delta has a specific policy for oversold flights. According to Rule 20 of the Domestic General Rules Tariff:

A) Before denying boarding to any passenger holding a confirmed reservation on an oversold flight, Delta will ask other passengers on the flight to voluntarily give up their seat in exchange for compensation [1].

B) If there are more volunteers than required, selection of the volunteer(s) to receive compensation will be determined in Delta’s sole discretion. If an insufficient number of passengers volunteer, Delta may involuntarily deny boarding according to the following boarding priority rules: 
1) Passengers holding tickets for travel in premium cabin, SkyMiles members with certain elite-status designations, and passengers holding tickets purchased under a D [1].

C) Involuntary denied boarding passengers will be transported on Delta’s next flight on which seats are available in the class of service originally purchased. At Delta's sole discretion, they may also travel on another carrier or via ground transportation, possibly in a lower class of service with potential for partial refund [4].

RULE 20: DENIED BOARDING COMPENSATION A) Overbooking of Flights
Because passengers with confirmed reservations on a flight sometimes fail to show, Delta reserves
the right to sell more tickets for travel on each flight than there are seats available on the aircraft.
In some cases, this may result in a flight in which Delta cannot accommodate one or more
passengers with confirmed reservations (an “oversold flight”). Delta may deny boarding to
passengers with confirmed reservations on an oversold flight as set forth in this rule. The rights of
passengers who are denied boarding shall be governed by this Rule.
B) Request For Volunteers
Before denying boarding to any passenger holding a confirmed reservation on an oversold flight,
Delta will ask other passengers on the flight to voluntarily give up their seat in exchange for
compensation in an amount and form to be determined by Delta in its sole discretion. If a sufficient
number of volunteers agree to give up their seats in response to Delta’s offer, then no passenger
with a confirmed reservation will be involuntarily denied boarding due to the oversale of the flight.
If there are more volunteers than required, selection of the volunteer(s) to receive compensation
will be determined in Delta’s sole discretion.
C) Involuntary Denied Boarding
If an insufficient number of passengers volunteer to give up their seats in response to Delta’s offer,
Delta may involuntarily deny boarding to one or more passengers on the oversold flight according
to the following boarding priority rules:
1) Passengers Holding Tickets for Travel in Premium Cabin, SkyMiles members identified
with a Diamond Medallion (“DM”), Platinum Medallion (“PM”), or Gold Medallion (“GM”)
elite-status designation, and passengers holding tickets purchased under a DL corporate
travel agreement.
Passengers holding tickets for confirmed space in the First or Business class cabin,
SkyMiles members identified with a DM, PM, or GM elite-status designation, and
passengers holding tickets purchased under a DL corporate travel agreement will be
accommodated before other passengers holding tickets and/or boarding passes for
confirmed space in the Coach cabin.
2) Passengers With Boarding Passes
Subject to the terms set forth in Rule 20(c)(1) and (4), passengers holding boarding passes
who check in and present themselves at the departure gate in compliance with Rule 13
will be accommodated before passengers traveling in the same cabin who have not been
issued boarding passes or who fail to comply with applicable check-in requirements.
Subject to the availability of seats on the aircraft, boarding passes may be obtained by
passengers who hold tickets for confirmed reserved space in the following manner:
a) for passengers traveling on electronic tickets, through the Online Check-in feature on
Delta.com within 24 hours of scheduled departure;
b) for passengers traveling on electronic tickets, through a Delta airport kiosk within four
hours of scheduled departure; or
c) from a Delta airport ticket counter and/or the check-in desk located in the departure
area.
3) Passengers Without Boarding Passes
Passengers with confirmed reservations who have not been issued a boarding pass and
present themselves at the departure gate in compliance with Rule 13 will be
accommodated according to the following priority rules:
a) Passengers who have been rebooked to the present flight as a result of an irregular operation (e.g., delay, cancellation) of a previously booked flight.
b) SkyMiles members identified with a Silver Medallion (“FO”) elite-status designation.
c) Passengers with a SkyTeam Elite or Elite Plus status.
d) Passengers without any elite-status designation.
Within each of the foregoing groups, passengers are prioritized first by class of service
and then by time of check-in.

question: What are the rules for shipping cargo domestically with Delta?
answer:
Delta's domestic shipping rules cover various aspects of cargo transportation. Here are some key points:

1. **Applicability and Definitions**:
   - The rules apply to transportation between points served within the United States by Delta [3].
   - "Air Waybill" refers to Uniform Air Waybill, International Air Waybill/Consignment Note, or other non-negotiable shipping documents issued by the carrier [1].

2. **Acceptance and Carriage of Live Animals**:
   - Live warm-blooded animals can be accepted as “DASH” (a premium product) up to 100 pounds or as a "Standard" product.
   - Requirements for live animals must comply with government regulations, and advance arrangements are required [3].
   - Pug and snub-nosed breeds will not be accepted if the temperature exceeds 75 degrees Fahrenheit/24 degrees Celsius during any part of their journey. Examples include Boston Terrier, Brussels Griffin, Dutch Pug, Japanese Spaniel (Japanese Chin), Japanese Pug, Pekingese, Shih Tzu, Staffordshire Bull Terrier [3].
   - Live wild birds can only be shipped to or from a zoo, sanctuary, preserve, government wildlife agency, or rehabilitation center and must be born or bred in captivity on special farms. Transportation is restricted to Delta's online service [3].

3. **Shipment Acceptability**:
   - Shipments must comply with all rules and regulations of the tariffs and applicable laws, ordinances, and governmental rules [3].

4. **Air Waybill and Shipping Documents**:
   - The shipper must present a non-negotiable air waybill or other shipping document issued by Delta for each shipment [4].
   - Statements in the air waybill regarding weight, dimensions, packing, number of packages are considered prima facie evidence unless checked by the carrier in the presence of the shipper.
   - The air waybill and applicable rules will apply throughout the handling of the shipment by or for the carrier [4].

5. **Perishable Shipments**:
   - Perishable shipments that may decay or deteriorate due to temperature variations are subject to specific regulations [1].

6. **Interline Shipment**:
   - An interline shipment involves routing a shipment via two or more successive carriers [1].

7. **Legal Holiday**:
   - Legal holidays include national, state, provincial, and local legal holidays [1].

These rules ensure that cargo is handled according to Delta's standards and applicable regulations for domestic transportation.

question: Can I get a refund on a non-refundable Delta ticket?
answer:
Yes, you can request a refund for a non-refundable Delta ticket under certain conditions. According to Rule 22(B) of the Domestic Contract of Carriage [1], most tickets issued by Delta are nonrefundable. However, if you cancel or change your nonrefundable ticket prior to departure, subject to the applicable fare rules and other provisions of the Contract of Carriage, the value of the unused portion of a nonrefundable ticket (including taxes and government-imposed fees or charges), less applicable charges by Delta, may be applied toward the purchase of future travel on Delta, or to upgrade or downgrade those tickets after purchase. By cancelling or changing your ticket prior to departure, you authorize and consent to Delta receiving any available credit or refund of taxes and government-imposed fees or charges collected by Delta on the unused portion of the ticket [1]. Additionally, a fee may be deducted from any value available toward the purchase of future travel on Delta [1].

Furthermore, Rule 22(C) states that no refund will be issued unless Delta receives a request for the refund and any unused coupons are surrendered to Delta within one year of the original issue date of the ticket [1]. The form of refund is typically issued as follows: 
- For tickets paid by credit card, the refund will be issued to the credit card account used to purchase the ticket, usually within seven business days after Delta's initial receipt of the refund request [2].
- For tickets paid by cash (if accepted), a check will be issued to the person named as a passenger on the ticket, typically within 20 days after Delta's receipt of the initial refund request [2].

It is also important to note that claims for overcharges are not valid if made more than 45 days after the date of issue of the ticket [3].
